Hi Jordan & Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on priorities and the expected integration pattern. As promised, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) capturing milestones, owners, target dates, and dependencies. High level summary below:

- Discovery complete (✓) — Marissa / Acme
- MAP draft shared — Marissa (today)
- Technical scoping and SOW alignment — Lauren & Acme eng (target: 2026-12-08)
- Procurement / PO issuance — Acme procurement (target: 2026-12-15)
- Legal review (MSA/DPA/SLA) — see notes below (target: 2026-12-10)
- Final signature & kickoff — target close date: 2026-12-22

MAP milestone: Legal redlines (MSA / DPA / SLA) — questions for you: who will own initial edits/redlines on your side, and what turnaround times do you prefer? Our suggested approach (to keep momentum):

1) Acme legal submits redlines (Word tracked changes) for MSA + any DPA asks — target: within 3 business days of receiving the MAP (i.e., by 2026-11-30)
2) Redwood legal consolidates and returns a counter + comment matrix — target: 2 business days after receiving your redlines
3) SLA items (metrics/credits/ops) — Redwood typically owns the SLA template; customer to propose any deviations. Redwood legal will prioritize SLA counters within the same turnaround above.

If this timing works, please confirm and we will loop in Rishi from Legal to be the primary contact for consolidation and final review. Also attaching a short procurement checklist we use internally to speed PO submission.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.docx; procurement-instructions.pdf

Next steps: please confirm owners for Legal + Procurement and any dependencies we should add to the MAP. If you prefer, we can also accept a redline via Doc (Google suggestions) but tracked Word is easiest for contract teams.

Thanks — happy to sync quickly if helpful.

Best,

Jordan — great question. Looping in Rishi (Redwood Legal) to confirm, but our recommended and typical flow is below — this keeps versions tight and gives both sides SLA-like turnaround times so the deal can stay on the target close date.

Proposed ownership & turnaround times (suggested):

- Initial redlines: Acme Legal to submit tracked Word redlines for MSA + DPA (owner: Acme Legal). Target: 3 business days from receipt.
- Consolidation & response: Redwood Legal (primary: Rishi) will consolidate, produce a single redline + comment matrix, and return to Acme. Target: 2 business days after receiving your redlines.
- SLA negotiation: Redwood will provide a standard SLA template as baseline. If Acme proposes SLA-specific edits (metrics/credits/MTTR), Redwood Legal + Product will review and respond. Target: initial SLA counter within 3 business days; subsequent rounds 2-3 business days per round.
- Data residency / security exceptions: These are treated as escalations — Redwood Security will review; if changes are required to the DPA, Redwood will aim for 3-5 business day turnaround depending on scope.

Ownership: Rishi will be the Redwood owner for legal consolidation and final signoff. Lauren will continue to own technical scoping and will document any dependencies that affect SLA/ops. Vivek is on-hand for customer success & operational questions.

Process notes:
- Preferred format: tracked Word for initial redlines; a short comment matrix (one-pager) is very helpful for key asks.
- We can accept Google suggestions if your team prefers, but Word with tracked changes is fastest for legal teams.
- For signature, we can do DocuSign. I'll add a HubSpot task for signature + procurement once legal is close.

Rishi — can you confirm turnaround is OK from your side? Jordan/Priya — if that flow works, please send your redlines and we'll start the clock.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
